summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on PR #449 by triaging, implementing fixes, running tests, and replying to each thread.
summary.outcome: All 6 review threads triaged and addressed: 4 code fixes implemented across 5 files, 1 thread marked not applicable, all tests passing (71 IPNS service + 23 parser), committed and pushed.

repo: cipher-box is a monorepo with Rust (apps/desktop/src-tauri, crates/fuse), TypeScript NestJS API (apps/api), and GitHub Actions E2E workflows
IPNS record parsing logic lives in apps/api/src/ipns/ipns-record-parser.ts with group scanning that lacked bounds checks
The desktop-e2e workflow starts the API with 'node dist/main.js &' and log collection needed a file redirect to capture API output
PublishCoordinator is in crates/fuse, not apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs — seeding serves as fallback when resolve fails (intentional design)

code.finding: Parse failure in fuse mod was silently ignored; fix added warning log at two locations
CID mismatch on cached record resolution was not logged; added warning log
Group scanning lacked bounds checks, risking out-of-bounds reads; fixed with explicit bounds validation
Test for sequence number mismatch case was missing; added to the existing describe block for resolve tests
API process started without stdout/stderr redirect, making log collection in CI impossible; fixed by redirecting to a log file

workflow: GraphQL reviewThreads query used to fetch unresolved PR threads; REST used for replies (in_reply_to must be integer, use --field not -f)
Resolve threads via GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation after replying
pnpm test and cargo check both used to validate fixes before committing

friction: Finding PublishCoordinator required multiple grep attempts across different paths before locating it in crates/fuse rather than the fuse mod.rs file
Needed several reads of the large ipns.service.spec.ts to locate the right insertion point for the new test
open_items: Thread 2 (mod.rs:226) marked not applicable — seeding-as-fallback behavior may warrant a follow-up design discussion if the pattern causes confusion for future reviewers
